module.title: Unit 8: Office Health, Safety & Ergonomic Regulations
module.objective: Mampu memahami dan menyusun panduan keselamatan kerja menggunakan modal obligation (must, have to, should).

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Office Safety and Ergonomics
subModules.grammarFocus: Modals of Obligation and Advice (must, have to, should, ought to, had better)
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Workplace Safety, Ergonomics, and Emergency Procedures

content.summary: In this mission, you will read an office safety handbook. You will learn how modern workplaces describe health rules, ergonomic habits, and emergency procedures using modals of obligation and advice.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Modal verbs of obligation and prohibition (must, must not, have to, don't have to) and advice (should, ought to, had better)
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Health and safety terms such as hazard, workstation, compliance, ergonomic, and evacuation
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning safety manuals for specific requirements and distinguishing between strict rules and practical recommendations

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a workplace safety and ergonomics handbook.
Locate specific details about workstation setup and fire emergency procedures.
Distinguish clearly between obligations, prohibitions, and recommendations.

contextWarmup.prompt: Imagine your office chair causes lower back pain after two hours of typing. What is the most appropriate action based on standard workplace advice?
options: Adjust your chair height and ask for an ergonomic assessment.
Ignore the pain because office workers do not have a choice.
Leave the office immediately without telling your supervisor.
contextWarmup.explanation: Workplace guidelines recommend adjusting your chair and reporting discomfort so the company can provide proper ergonomic support.

rules: Rule 1: Use 'must' for strong personal or internal rules, and 'must not' for strict prohibitions where something is strictly forbidden.
Rule 2: Use 'have to' for external laws, company policies, and official regulations. Use 'don't have to' when something is optional rather than forbidden.
Rule 3: Use 'should' or 'ought to' for sensible advice. Use 'had better' for urgent warnings with negative consequences if ignored.

commonTrap.explanation: 'Must not' means an action is completely prohibited. 'Don't have to' means the action is optional and not necessary. Confusing them changes a strict ban into optional advice.
commonTrap.wrong: You don't have to block the fire exit doors.
commonTrap.correct: You must not block the fire exit doors.

content.passageTitle: Apex Logistics Office Safety and Ergonomics Guide
paragraphs: Welcome to your new office at Apex Logistics. Our company takes workplace well-being seriously. Every employee must follow our safety guidelines to keep our building safe and comfortable. If you notice any hazard, such as loose electrical wires or wet tiles in the hallway, you must report it to the facilities team immediately. Regular inspections help us maintain full compliance with national safety laws.

Your daily comfort also depends on how you set up your workstation. You ought to adjust your chair height so that your feet rest flat on the floor. Your computer screen should be at eye level, roughly an arm's length away. Good posture prevents back pain, and taking short screen breaks every hour prevents eye strain. You do not have to buy special equipment yourself because the company provides ergonomic keyboards and wrist rests upon request.

Emergency preparedness is another vital part of our culture. All staff members have to take part in our fire drill twice a year. During an evacuation, you must leave personal items behind and follow the green exit signs to the assembly point outside. You should also locate the nearest first-aid kit on your floor today. You had better pay attention to these instructions, as quick actions save lives during real emergencies.

questions.question: What must employees do if they spot loose wires in the hallway?
options: Fix the wires themselves with office tape.
Report the problem to the facilities team immediately.
Ignore the issue until the next monthly inspection.
questions.answer: Report the problem to the facilities team immediately.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that employees must report hazards like loose wires to the facilities team immediately.

questions.question: Why does Apex Logistics perform regular safety inspections?
options: To keep full compliance with national safety laws.
To monitor whether staff arrive at work on time.
To see if employees are using their phones at work.
questions.answer: To keep full compliance with national safety laws.
questions.explanation: The text explains that regular inspections help the company maintain compliance with national safety laws.

questions.question: Where should your computer monitor be placed for healthy ergonomic alignment?
options: Below your desk surface to protect your neck.
At eye level, approximately an arm's length away.
As close to your face as possible to read small fonts.
questions.answer: At eye level, approximately an arm's length away.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states that your screen should be at eye level, roughly an arm's length away.

questions.question: How can staff members prevent eye strain during the workday?
options: By turning off the office lights completely.
By taking short screen breaks every hour.
By working without a chair while standing on one foot.
questions.answer: By taking short screen breaks every hour.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 specifically mentions that taking short screen breaks every hour prevents eye strain.

questions.question: What does the text say about getting ergonomic accessories like wrist rests?
options: Staff members must buy them from an approved shop.
Employees do not have to buy them because the company provides them on request.
Only senior managers are permitted to use wrist rests.
questions.answer: Employees do not have to buy them because the company provides them on request.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says employees do not have to buy special equipment because the company supplies it upon request.

questions.question: How often are employees required to join a fire drill?
options: Twice every month.
Once every two years.
Twice a year.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 clearly states that all staff members have to take part in the fire drill twice a year.

questions.question: What must people do with their personal bags and coats during an evacuation?
options: Leave personal items behind and follow the exit signs.
Pack everything carefully into a secure locker.
Carry all heavy equipment to the outside parking lot.
questions.answer: Leave personal items behind and follow the exit signs.
questions.explanation: The text directs staff to leave personal items behind and follow green exit signs during an evacuation.

questions.question: What does 'you do not have to buy' mean in the second paragraph?
options: Buying special items is strictly prohibited by law.
Buying special items is not necessary because they are provided.
Buying special items is a mandatory duty for all staff.
questions.answer: Buying special items is not necessary because they are provided.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' expresses lack of obligation or necessity, meaning you can do it, but it is not required.

questions.question: Why does the writer use 'had better pay attention' in the final sentence?
options: To give a casual suggestion that can be ignored.
To give a strong warning because ignoring safety rules can endanger lives.
To ask employees to write an essay about emergency drills.
questions.answer: To give a strong warning because ignoring safety rules can endanger lives.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' signals a strong recommendation or warning with severe consequences if not followed.

questions.question: Which action supports good posture while working at a desk?
options: Adjusting your chair so your feet rest flat on the floor.
Crossing your legs and leaning forward toward the monitor.
Sitting on the edge of the desk instead of using a chair.
questions.answer: Adjusting your chair so your feet rest flat on the floor.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 instructs employees to adjust their chair height so that their feet rest flat on the floor.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Office Safety and Posture Check

content.summary: Learn how to spot spoken obligations, recommendations, and ergonomic safety instructions in a modern workplace setting.
learningObjectives: Catch the main rules during a workplace health orientation.
Distinguish strong obligations like 'must' from recommendations like 'should'.
Identify sound linking and reductions in everyday workplace speech.

keyPhrases.note: Used when reviewing standard procedures or checklists.
Expresses a strict prohibition for safety purposes.
Standard ergonomic guideline for positioning computer screens.
A routine practice simulation for emergency building evacuations.

connectedSpeech.note: The voiced /v/ sound changes to voiceless /f/ before the voiceless consonant /t/.
The /t/ in 'must' is dropped before the nasal consonant /n/.
The final /t/ and initial /j/ merge to form a crisp /tʃ/ sound.
The preposition 'to' reduces to a short schwa vowel /ə/ in natural speech.

lines.text: Do we have regular fire drills?

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Drafting Workplace Safety and Ergonomic Guidelines

content.summary: This guide demonstrates how to write clear workplace policies, ergonomic guidelines, and safety warnings using modals of obligation, prohibition, and advice.

blueprintItems.title: Formula 1: Direct Rules and Absolute Prohibitions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + must / must not + base verb + complement
blueprintItems.example: All employees must keep emergency exit routes clear at all times.

blueprintItems.title: Formula 2: External Regulations and Lack of Obligation
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + have to / don't have to + base verb + complement
blueprintItems.example: Desk workers do not have to wear helmets, but they have to display their security badges.

blueprintItems.title: Formula 3: Ergonomic Advice and Urgent Warnings
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + should / ought to / had better (not) + base verb + complement
blueprintItems.example: You had better replace damaged cords before using your desktop workstation.

mechanicsRules.rule: Never confuse 'must not' (prohibition) with 'do not have to' (absence of obligation).
mechanicsRules.badExample: You do not have to block the fire door because it is forbidden.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: You must not block the fire door because it is forbidden.
mechanicsRules.why: 'Must not' means an action is strictly against the rules. 'Do not have to' means an action is optional.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always use the bare infinitive without 'to' after modal verbs like 'must', 'should', and 'had better'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Workers had better to adjust their chair heights every morning.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Workers had better adjust their chair heights every morning.
mechanicsRules.why: Modal auxiliaries take the base form of the verb directly, except for 'ought to' and 'have to'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after introductory conditional clauses in health and safety instructions.
mechanicsRules.badExample: If your monitor flickers you should report it to IT support.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: If your monitor flickers, you should report it to IT support.
mechanicsRules.why: A dependent conditional clause placed at the start of a sentence requires a comma before the main clause.

sampleSentences.en: Staff members must report any office hazard to their safety representative immediately.
sampleSentences.id: Anggota staf harus segera melaporkan bahaya kantor apa pun kepada perwakilan keselamatan mereka.

sampleSentences.en: You don't have to turn off your computer every break, but you must lock your screen.
sampleSentences.id: Anda tidak perlu mematikan komputer Anda setiap istirahat, tetapi Anda wajib mengunci layar Anda.
sampleSentences.focus: Contrasting lack of obligation with an official rule

sampleSentences.en: Office staff ought to position their monitors at eye level to prevent neck pain.
sampleSentences.id: Staf kantor sebaiknya memposisikan monitor mereka sejajar dengan mata untuk mencegah sakit leher.

sampleSentences.en: You had better not leave loose cables across the walkways.
sampleSentences.id: Anda sebaiknya tidak meninggalkan kabel yang menjuntai di sepanjang jalur pejalan kaki.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: workers must to wear protective glasses near the server racks
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Workers must wear protective glasses near the server racks.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Pekerja harus memakai kacamata pelindung di dekat rak server.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Do not insert 'to' after the modal 'must', and capitalize the first word of the sentence.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: if you feel eye strain you should rest your eyes for ten minutes
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: If you feel eye strain, you should rest your eyes for ten minutes.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Jika Anda merasa mata lelah, Anda sebaiknya mengistirahatkan mata Anda selama sepuluh menit.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Place a comma after the introductory 'if' clause and capitalize the first word.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: you had better not leaves wet umbrellas on the wooden floor mr green
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: You had better not leave wet umbrellas on the wooden floor, Mr. Green.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Anda sebaiknya tidak meninggalkan payung basah di lantai kayu, Tuan Green.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use the base verb after 'had better not', add a comma before direct address, and capitalize formal titles and names.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Write an Ergonomic Setup Advisory
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three to four sentences advising a colleague on how to set up their office workstation properly. Use 'should' or 'ought to' for posture advice, and mention chair adjustments or screen position.
guidedLabChallenges.example: You should position your computer screen at eye level. You ought to keep your feet flat on the floor while sitting. You also need to adjust your armrests so your shoulders stay relaxed.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Write your ergonomic workstation advice here...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Draft Office Safety Rules
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four sentences describing two mandatory office rules and two actions that are optional. Use 'must / must not' and 'don't have to' correctly.
guidedLabChallenges.example: All employees must keep fire exits completely clear of boxes. Staff must not plug too many heaters into one socket. You do not have to shut down your computer at noon, but you have to turn off the lights when leaving.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into a direct rule using 'must not':
practicumQuestions.promptText: It is strictly forbidden for staff to block the emergency exit paths.
targetAnswers: Staff must not block the emergency exit paths.
Staff members must not block the emergency exit paths.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To state a strict rule or prohibition, use 'must not' followed directly by the base verb 'block'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using 'don't have to' to show that an action is optional:
practicumQuestions.promptText: It is not necessary for employees to print their safety manuals.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Employees don't have to...' or 'Employees do not have to...'
targetAnswers: Employees don't have to print their safety manuals.
Employees do not have to print their safety manuals.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Don't have to' expresses a lack of obligation, showing that printing the manual is optional.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence into an urgent warning using 'had better not':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Do not ignore the flickering monitor, or you will get a headache.
targetAnswers: You had better not ignore the flickering monitor, or you will get a headache.
You had better not ignore the flickering monitor.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Had better not' gives a strong warning about negative consequences when an action is taken.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences into one using the connector 'so that':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Adjust your chair height. Your elbows rest comfortably on the desk.
practicumQuestions.hint: Join the clauses with 'so that' to explain purpose.
targetAnswers: Adjust your chair height so that your elbows rest comfortably on the desk.
Adjust your chair height, so that your elbows rest comfortably on the desk.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'so that' to link an instruction with its intended ergonomic purpose.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences into one using 'because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Staff must not overload electrical power strips. They can cause an electrical fire.
practicumQuestions.hint: Put 'because' between the prohibition and the reason.
targetAnswers: Staff must not overload electrical power strips because they can cause an electrical fire.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Connect the safety prohibition directly to the reason using the causal conjunction 'because'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the modal verb error and punctuation in this safety notice:
practicumQuestions.promptText: employees must to inspect their computer chairs once a year
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove 'to' after the modal and capitalize the first word.
targetAnswers: Employees must inspect their computer chairs once a year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The modal auxiliary 'must' is followed immediately by the base verb 'inspect' without 'to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Add proper punctuation and capitalization to this conditional guideline:
practicumQuestions.promptText: if you experience wrist discomfort you should visit the company doctor
practicumQuestions.hint: Add a comma after the 'if' clause and capitalize the first letter.
targetAnswers: If you experience wrist discomfort, you should visit the company doctor.
practicumQuestions.explanation: When an 'if' clause introduces a sentence, it must be separated from the main clause by a comma.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the sentence to express an external regulation using 'have to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Company policy requires all new workers to attend an ergonomics workshop.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin with 'All new workers have to...'
targetAnswers: All new workers have to attend an ergonomics workshop.
New workers have to attend an ergonomics workshop.
practicumQuestions.explanation: External policies and institutional requirements are expressed naturally using 'have to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite this recommendation using 'ought to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: It is advisable for office workers to take a short screen break every hour.
targetAnswers: Office workers ought to take a short screen break every hour.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses formal advice or sensible recommendations, matching the meaning of 'advisable'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write one complete sentence warning workers about wet hallway floors using 'had better' or 'must':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Draft a one-sentence safety instruction about a wet hallway floor.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'You must be careful...' or 'Workers had better watch their step...'
targetAnswers: Workers had better watch their step on the wet hallway floor.
You had better watch your step because the hallway floor is wet.
All employees must walk carefully because the hallway floor is wet.
You must be careful because the hallway floor is wet.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A clear warning or mandatory guideline must include a subject, a modal verb ('must' or 'had better'), a base verb, and a clear reason or location.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Office Health, Safety and Ergonomics

content.summary: In this lab, you learn how to give clear safety instructions, explain office guidelines, and discuss workstation setup using modals of obligation such as must, have to, and should.
content.audioGuidance: When giving instructions or warnings, use firm falling intonation on key content words. Stress the main verb or safety rule clearly so your listener understands the importance.

pillars.name: Modal Stress and Weak Forms
pillars.explanation: We often stress 'must' and 'must not' to emphasize strict rules. In contrast, 'have to' is often pronounced quickly as /hæf tu/ or /hæftə/, and 'should' is pronounced /ʃʊd/ with a soft, unstressed vowel unless you want to contrast advice.

pillars.name: Compound Noun Stress
pillars.target: Correct primary stress on compound terms
pillars.explanation: Safety terms like 'fire drill', 'first-aid kit', and 'workstation' place primary stress on the first element: FIRE drill, FIRST-aid kit, WORKstation.

pillars.name: Directives and Falling Intonation
pillars.explanation: When stating mandatory policies or pointing out workplace hazards, end your sentences with a falling pitch to sound confident and decisive.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress stays on the second syllable for both the verb and noun forms.
The stress remains firmly on the first syllable in both the noun and adjective forms.
The suffix '-ic' pulls the main stress forward onto the third syllable: er-go-NOM-ic.
The noun suffix '-tion' moves the primary stress to the syllable immediately before it.

drills.targetText: You must report every tripping hazard immediately.
drills.phonetic: /juː mʌst rɪˈpɔːt ˈevri ˈtrɪpɪŋ ˈhæzəd ɪˈmiːdiətli/
drills.focus: Strong modal 'must' and correct stress on 'hazard'
drills.hint: Put clear emphasis on 'must' and 'hazard', dropping your pitch at the end.

drills.targetText: Employees have to participate in the annual fire drill.
drills.phonetic: /ɪmˈplɔɪiːz hæf tuː pɑːˈtɪsɪpeɪt ɪn ði ˈænjuəl ˈfaɪə drɪl/
drills.focus: Weak form of 'have to' and compound stress on 'fire drill'
drills.hint: Blend 'have to' smoothly as /hæftə/ and stress 'fire' louder than 'drill'.

drills.targetText: You should adjust your workstation so the monitor sits at eye level.
drills.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd əˈdʒʌst jɔː ˈwɜːksteɪʃən səʊ ðə ˈmɒnɪtə sɪts æt aɪ ˈlevl/
drills.focus: Giving advice with 'should' and compound noun 'workstation'
drills.hint: Keep 'should' light and natural, focusing vocal energy on 'adjust' and 'workstation'.

drills.targetText: The safety officer ensures strict compliance with health regulations.
drills.phonetic: /ðə ˈseɪfti ˈɒfɪsə ɪnˈʃʊəz strɪkt kəmˈplaɪəns wɪð helθ ˌreɡjʊˈleɪʃənz/
drills.focus: Stress on second syllable of 'compliance' and rhythmic flow
drills.hint: Pronounce 'compliance' with clear second-syllable emphasis: com-PLI-ance.

roleplay.context: A safety coordinator is inspecting an office workspace and speaking to a team member about safety standards.

turns.speaker: Safety Coordinator
turns.text: Good morning. I noticed several cables stretched across the floor near your desk. That is a dangerous hazard.
turns.translation: Selamat pagi. Saya melihat beberapa kabel berserakan di lantai dekat meja Anda. Itu bahaya yang cukup berisiko.

turns.speaker: Team Member
turns.text: I apologize. I will tape them down immediately so nobody trips over them.
turns.translation: Saya minta maaf. Saya akan segera merekatkannya ke lantai agar tidak ada yang tersandung.

turns.speaker: Safety Coordinator
turns.text: Thank you. Remember that our company policy requires full compliance with walkway safety rules.
turns.translation: Terima kasih. Ingat bahwa kebijakan perusahaan kita mewajibkan kepatuhan penuh terhadap aturan keselamatan jalur jalan.

turns.speaker: Team Member
turns.text: Understood. I will also check where the nearest first-aid kit is located in case of emergencies.
turns.translation: Dimengerti. Saya juga akan memeriksa letak kotak P3K terdekat untuk situasi darurat.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 25 seconds about a workplace safety issue or hazard you experienced or noticed, and explain what actions were taken.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a safety hazard you once observed at work or school, and explain what people had to do to solve it.
storyPoints: Identify the hazard you saw, such as loose wires, wet floors, or blocked exits
Explain what employees or students had to do to stay safe
Describe the final outcome and how rules improved compliance
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I noticed loose power cables on the floor, so our manager told us we had to keep walkways clear to prevent injuries.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ ˈnəʊtɪst luːs ˈpaʊə ˈkeɪblz ɒn ðə flɔː/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use past tense alongside modal forms like 'had to' or 'should have' to narrate the incident clearly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 25 seconds explaining how you set up your workstation to avoid neck and back pain.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about your current workstation setup and what ergonomic changes you made to feel more comfortable.
storyPoints: Describe your desk and chair setup before making changes
Detail the ergonomic adjustments you made, including screen height and seating posture
State your advice on what everyone should do to prevent posture problems
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: To avoid back strain, I adjusted my ergonomic chair, lifted my monitor to eye level, and took regular breaks.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /tuː əˈvɔɪd bæk streɪn aɪ əˈdʒʌstɪd maɪ ˌɜːɡəˈnɒmɪk tʃeə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Focus on clear pronunciation of 'ergonomic' and explain your routine using modals like 'should' or 'ought to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are a floor warden giving safety instructions during an office orientation call. Respond to the new employee.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Welcome to our department! Can you remind me what we must do if we hear the fire alarm go off?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A new hire is asking the floor safety warden about emergency evacuation protocols during their first week.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: If you hear the alarm, you must leave the building immediately by the stairs and gather at the assembly point.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪf juː hɪə ði əˈlɑːm juː mʌst liːv ðə ˈbɪldɪŋ ɪˈmiːdiətli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the modal 'must' to state mandatory evacuation procedures clearly and with firm intonation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are an office manager advising a colleague who complains of severe wrist pain and neck stiffness.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: My wrists and neck hurt after typing all morning. Do you have any recommendations for my desk setup?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: An office manager advises a team member on adjusting desk equipment to meet ergonomic standards.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You should adjust your ergonomic chair and position your keyboard so your wrists stay flat while typing.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd əˈdʒʌst jɔː ˌɜːɡəˈnɒmɪk tʃeə ænd pəˈzɪʃən jɔː ˈkiːbɔːd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Offer constructive advice using 'should' or 'ought to' alongside ergonomic vocabulary.

practicumQuestions.instruction: A colleague asks where emergency medical supplies are kept. Tell them where the first-aid kit is located and what rules apply.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: One of our team members cut their hand on a sharp paper box. Where can I find basic medical supplies?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A colleague urgently asks you for medical materials after a minor cut occurs in the printing room.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You have to get the first-aid kit from the kitchen cabinet and report the injury to our safety supervisor.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /juː hæf tuː ɡet ðə ˈfɜːst eɪd kɪt frəm ðə ˈkɪtʃɪn ˈkæbɪnɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Express necessity with 'have to' and pronounce the compound term 'first-aid kit' with initial stress.

practicumQuestions.instruction: An intern is blocking an emergency exit with spare cardboard boxes. Explain the company rule firmly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: I just placed these supply boxes here for a few minutes while sorting files. Is that alright?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: An intern left storage boxes blocking a fire exit door in the corridor.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: No, you must not block the fire exit because it creates a serious hazard and breaks safety compliance rules.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /nəʊ juː mʌst nɒt blɒk ðə ˈfaɪər ˈeɡzɪt bɪˈkɒz ɪt kriːˈeɪts ə ˈsɪəriəs ˈhæzəd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'must not' to express strict prohibition with decisive falling intonation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence aloud, pronouncing the target vocabulary word 'ergonomic' and 'compliance' clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak the sentence: Our office bought ergonomic chairs to improve employee health and ensure compliance with labor laws.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Our office bought ergonomic chairs to improve employee health and ensure compliance with labor laws.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈaʊər ˈɒfɪs bɔːt ˌɜːɡəˈnɒmɪk tʃeəz tuː ɪmˈpruːv ɪmˈplɔɪiː helθ ænd ɪnˈʃʊə kəmˈplaɪəns wɪð ˈleɪbə lɔːz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Focus on the third syllable in 'er-go-NOM-ic' and the second syllable in 'com-PLI-ance'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence aloud, clearly emphasizing the obligation modals 'must' and 'have to'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak the sentence: You must wear safety boots in the warehouse, but you only have to wear regular shoes in the office.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You must wear safety boots in the warehouse, but you only have to wear regular shoes in the office.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /juː mʌst weə ˈseɪfti buːts ɪn ðə ˈweəhaʊs bʌt juː ˈəʊnli hæf tuː weə ˈreɡjʊlə ʃuːz ɪn ði ˈɒfɪs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Contrast the strong obligation 'must' with the routine obligation 'have to' using accurate intonation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the sentence aloud, placing correct primary stress on the compound nouns 'fire drill', 'first-aid kit', and 'workstation'.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak the sentence: After the fire drill, check your workstation and find the nearest first-aid kit.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: After the fire drill, check your workstation and find the nearest first-aid kit.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈɑːftə ðə ˈfaɪə drɪl tʃek jɔː ˈwɜːksteɪʃən ænd faɪnd ðə ˈnɪərɪst ˈfɜːst eɪd kɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Stress the first word of each compound noun: FIRE drill, WORKstation, FIRST-aid kit.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the question and directive pair aloud, using a rising intonation for the question and a falling intonation for the command.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak both parts: Do you see that hazard near the door? Move those cables right away.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Do you see that hazard near the door? Move those cables right away.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /duː juː siː ðæt ˈhæzəd nɪə ðə dɔː ↗ muːv ðəʊz ˈkeɪblz raɪt əˈweɪ ↘/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Rise your pitch at the end of the yes/no question 'door?' and lower your pitch firmly at the end of 'away.'.
